heuristics.rule: Apply for PGWP within 180 days of program completion confirmation
heuristics.condition: When a student has completed their program of study at a PGWP-eligible DLI
heuristics.action: Submit PGWP application within 180 days of receiving official confirmation of program completion
heuristics.because: Applications submitted after the 180-day window are ineligible; study permit must also have been valid at some point during those 180 days

heuristics.rule: Minimum 8-month program length required for PGWP eligibility (or 900 hours for Quebec programs)
heuristics.condition: When a student is assessing whether their completed program qualifies for a PGWP
heuristics.action: Confirm program length is at least 8 months (or 900 hours if in Quebec) at a PGWP-eligible DLI
heuristics.because: Programs shorter than 8 months (or 900 hours in Quebec) do not satisfy the minimum duration requirement for PGWP eligibility

heuristics.rule: PGWP valid for 3 years if program is 2 years or more, or if program is a master's or doctoral degree of any length
heuristics.condition: When a student completes a program of 2 years or more, or a master's or doctoral degree
heuristics.because: IRCC ties PGWP length to study program length; master's/doctoral programs receive 3 years regardless of duration since February 2024 rule change
heuristics.regulatory_basis: IRCC PGWP eligibility — canada.ca (February 2024 rule change)

heuristics.rule: PGWP duration equals program length for programs 8 months to less than 2 years
heuristics.condition: When a student completes a program between 8 months and less than 2 years
heuristics.action: Expect PGWP valid for the same duration as the program length
heuristics.because: IRCC policy ties PGWP length directly to study program duration for sub-2-year programs

heuristics.rule: At least 50% of program must be completed in class within Canada for lock-in dates on or after September 1, 2024
heuristics.condition: When a student's lock-in date is on or after September 1, 2024 and they completed any portion of their program outside Canada
heuristics.action: Ensure at least 50% of the program was completed in class within Canada; time studied outside Canada will be deducted from PGWP length
heuristics.because: Distance learning outside Canada reduces PGWP validity and failure to meet the 50% in-Canada in-class threshold renders the student ineligible

heuristics.rule: For lock-in dates between September 1, 2022 and August 31, 2024, at least 50% of program must be completed within Canada (online or in class)
heuristics.condition: When a student's lock-in date falls between September 1, 2022 and August 31, 2024
heuristics.action: Confirm at least 50% of the program was completed within Canada; online study from outside Canada before August 31, 2024 counts toward PGWP length only if it constitutes less than 50% of the program
heuristics.because: Transitional rules distinguish between in-Canada online study and outside-Canada online study for PGWP length calculation

heuristics.rule: Transfers from non-DLI to DLI: only time at the DLI counts toward the 8-month minimum
heuristics.condition: When a student transferred from a non-DLI institution to a DLI
heuristics.action: Count only the time spent at the DLI; must be at least 8 months at the DLI to be eligible
heuristics.because: Non-DLI study time is not creditable toward PGWP eligibility even if the student later transfers to a qualifying DLI

heuristics.rule: Accelerated program completion may still yield PGWP for full normal program length
heuristics.condition: When a student completes their study program in less time than the normal program length
heuristics.action: Apply for PGWP valid for the full normal length of the program (not the accelerated completion time)
heuristics.because: IRCC policy allows PGWP duration based on the normal program length even when completion was accelerated

heuristics.rule: Programs with an overseas component: PGWP valid only for time studied in Canada
heuristics.condition: When a student's Canadian program includes an overseas component
heuristics.action: Calculate PGWP duration based only on time studied in Canada, excluding the overseas portion
heuristics.because: IRCC policy explicitly excludes overseas study time from PGWP length calculations

heuristics.rule: Language requirement: CLB/NCLC 7 in all four skills required for degree, college diploma, and graduate certificate programs
heuristics.condition: When a student completed a bachelor's, master's, doctoral degree, college diploma, or graduate certificate and is applying for a PGWP
heuristics.action: Prove English or French language proficiency at minimum CLB/NCLC 7 in reading, writing, listening, and speaking
heuristics.because: Failure to meet language threshold is an explicit PGWP eligibility disqualifier for these program types

heuristics.rule: Field of study must be in an IRCC-eligible field for degree, college diploma, and graduate certificate programs
heuristics.condition: When a student completed a bachelor's, master's, doctoral degree, college diploma, or graduate certificate
heuristics.action: Verify that the program's field of study is on IRCC's list of eligible fields of study
heuristics.because: Programs in non-eligible fields of study do not satisfy PGWP requirements for these program types

decision_factors.why_it_matters: Determines both basic PGWP eligibility (minimum 8 months / 900 hours in Quebec) and the duration of the PGWP issued
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Check total program length: under 8 months = ineligible; 8 months to less than 2 years = PGWP equals program length; 2 years or more = 3-year PGWP; master's or doctoral (any length) = 3-year PGWP

decision_factors.why_it_matters: A student must have completed their program at a PGWP-eligible designated learning institution; non-eligible DLIs disqualify the applicant
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Confirm the institution is on IRCC's list of PGWP-eligible DLIs at the time of study

decision_factors.why_it_matters: Students must have maintained full-time status during each semester; part-time is only allowed in the final semester
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Review enrollment records for each semester; any non-final semester with part-time status may disqualify

decision_factors.why_it_matters: PGWP application must be submitted within 180 days of program completion confirmation; missing this window forfeits eligibility
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Identify the official date of program completion confirmation and count forward 180 days

decision_factors.factor: Study permit validity during 180-day post-completion period
decision_factors.why_it_matters: The study permit must have been valid at some point during the 180 days after program completion
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Confirm study permit expiry date overlaps with the 180-day post-completion window

decision_factors.factor: Proportion of program completed in Canada vs. outside Canada
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Studying more than 50% of the program outside Canada (or via distance learning) results in ineligibility or reduced PGWP length depending on the lock-in date
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Calculate percentage of program completed within Canada; check lock-in date to determine applicable rule (pre/post September 1, 2024)

decision_factors.why_it_matters: For degree, college diploma, and graduate certificate programs, the program must be in an IRCC-eligible field of study
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Cross-reference program field against IRCC's eligible fields of study list

decision_factors.why_it_matters: Applicants for degree, college diploma, and graduate certificate programs must demonstrate minimum CLB/NCLC 7 in all four language skills
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Submit approved language test results showing CLB/NCLC 7 or higher in reading, writing, listening, and speaking

decision_factors.factor: Whether student has previously received a PGWP
decision_factors.why_it_matters: A student who has already received a PGWP is categorically ineligible for another
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Check immigration history for any prior PGWP issuance

decision_factors.why_it_matters: Programs delivered by a private career college under a public institution's name are generally not PGWP-eligible, with narrow time-limited exceptions
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Determine if the program was delivered under a curriculum licensing agreement; check program start date against the applicable exception deadline (May 15, 2024 for same-province; January 31, 2023 for inter-province)

decision_factors.factor: Source of funding (government scholarship requiring return home)
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Students who received GAC funding or scholarships requiring return to their home country after graduation are explicitly ineligible
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Review scholarship or funding terms for repatriation requirements

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Completing a program through significant distance/online learning outside Canada
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: Time studied outside Canada is deducted from PGWP length (for lock-in dates on or after September 1, 2024), potentially reducing a 2-year program's associated PGWP below 3 years or even below eligibility threshold
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: Students who studied partially abroad or completed online segments from outside Canada after September 1, 2024

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Enrolling in a program delivered by a private college under a public institution's curriculum licensing agreement
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: The program is generally NOT PGWP-eligible despite being associated with a public institution name; narrow exceptions only apply to programs started before May 15, 2024 (same province) or January 31, 2023 (cross-province)
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: Students who enrolled in private career college programs branded under public institution partnerships after the cutoff dates

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Studying part-time in any semester other than the final semester
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: Part-time enrollment in non-final semesters violates the full-time status requirement and can disqualify the student from PGWP eligibility entirely
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: Students who reduced course loads due to work, health, or personal circumstances in non-final semesters

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Completing a Canadian program with an overseas study component
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: The PGWP will only be valid for the time studied in Canada; the overseas portion does not count toward PGWP duration, potentially shortening the permit significantly
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: Students in exchange programs or programs with mandatory international components

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Transferring from a non-DLI institution to a DLI
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: Only the time spent at the DLI counts toward the 8-month minimum; prior studies at the non-DLI are entirely excluded from the PGWP eligibility calculation
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: Students who spent significant time at a non-DLI institution before transferring

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Accepting a government scholarship with a repatriation requirement (e.g., GAC funding)
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: Accepting such funding categorically disqualifies the student from PGWP eligibility regardless of other criteria met
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: Students who accepted government-funded awards without reading post-graduation conditions

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Completing an accelerated program faster than its normal duration
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: While the PGWP may be valid for the full normal program length, the student still must apply within 180 days of actual completion — the earlier completion date starts the clock, not the normal program end date
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: Students in accelerated programs who may not realize their 180-day window opens earlier than classmates on standard timelines

failure_patterns.pattern: Applying for a PGWP after the 180-day post-completion window has expired
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: Students may be unaware that the 180-day clock starts from the date of official program completion confirmation, not from a subjective awareness of completion
failure_patterns.consequence: PGWP application ineligibility; student cannot obtain a PGWP
warning_signs: Student delays applying while waiting for official transcripts or final grades
Student is unaware of the exact date their institution issued program completion confirmation

failure_patterns.pattern: Completing more than 50% of the program through distance learning or outside Canada
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: Students who enrolled during pandemic-era flexibility or studied abroad exceed the allowable distance learning threshold
failure_patterns.consequence: PGWP ineligibility (program completed over 50% through distance learning is an explicit disqualifier)
warning_signs: Majority of courses were online from a location outside Canada
Student spent extended periods outside Canada during their study program

failure_patterns.pattern: Attending a private college program delivered under a public institution's curriculum licensing agreement after the cutoff dates
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: Students enroll assuming the public institution's name on the program confers PGWP eligibility without verifying the delivery model
failure_patterns.consequence: PGWP ineligibility; the program is not PGWP-eligible if started after May 15, 2024 (same province) or January 31, 2023 (cross-province)
warning_signs: Program is physically delivered at a private career college campus
Tuition or administrative correspondence comes from a private institution despite the public institution branding

failure_patterns.pattern: Studying part-time during a non-final semester
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: Students reduce course loads for personal, financial, or health reasons without understanding it violates PGWP full-time status requirements
failure_patterns.consequence: PGWP ineligibility due to failure to maintain full-time status throughout the program
warning_signs: Enrollment records show below full-time credit load in a non-final semester
Student took a reduced load semester mid-program

failure_patterns.pattern: Transferring from a non-DLI to a DLI but spending less than 8 months at the DLI
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: Students assume their total combined study time counts; only time at the DLI is creditable
failure_patterns.consequence: PGWP ineligibility; minimum 8 months at the DLI not met
warning_signs: Total study time in Canada exceeds 8 months but less than 8 months was at a DLI
Student transferred to a DLI late in their program

failure_patterns.pattern: Applying for a second PGWP after having already received one
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: Students complete an additional Canadian program and assume a second PGWP is available
failure_patterns.consequence: PGWP ineligibility; individuals who already received a PGWP are categorically excluded
warning_signs: Student has prior Canadian immigration history showing a PGWP was issued
Student returning to Canada for a second degree after using PGWP from a first degree

diagnostic_questions.question: Was the program completed at a PGWP-eligible designated learning institution (DLI)?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the institution meets the foundational eligibility requirement for PGWP
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Proceed to assess program length, field of study, and other requirements
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Student is categorically ineligible for a PGWP

diagnostic_questions.question: Was the program at least 8 months long (or 900 hours for Quebec programs)?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the program meets the minimum duration threshold for PGWP eligibility
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Proceed to assess PGWP duration based on program length
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Student is ineligible for a PGWP

diagnostic_questions.question: Did the student maintain full-time status in every semester except possibly the final semester?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the student meets the continuous full-time enrollment requirement
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Proceed to assess other eligibility criteria
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Student may be ineligible unless part-time was only in the final semester

diagnostic_questions.question: Is the application being submitted within 180 days of official program completion confirmation?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the application falls within the mandatory filing window
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Confirm study permit was also valid at some point during the 180-day post-completion period
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Student is ineligible; the 180-day window has expired

diagnostic_questions.question: Was the study permit valid at any point during the 180 days after program completion?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the student's legal study status was maintained through the post-completion period
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Student is ineligible for a PGWP

diagnostic_questions.question: Did the student complete more than 50% of the program through distance learning or outside Canada?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the student exceeds the distance learning threshold that disqualifies PGWP eligibility
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Student is ineligible for a PGWP
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Proceed; also assess whether any time outside Canada must be deducted from PGWP duration under applicable lock-in date rules

diagnostic_questions.question: Has the student previously received a PGWP?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the categorical one-time-only restriction applies
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Student is categorically ineligible for another PGWP
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Proceed to assess remaining eligibility criteria

diagnostic_questions.question: Was the program delivered by a private career college under a curriculum licensing agreement with a public institution?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the public-private partnership exception rules apply and whether the program is PGWP-eligible
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Check program start date against applicable cutoff (May 15, 2024 for same-province; January 31, 2023 for inter-province); programs started after these dates are not PGWP-eligible
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Proceed with standard DLI eligibility assessment

diagnostic_questions.question: Did the student receive GAC funding or a scholarship requiring return to their home country after graduation?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether a government funding condition categorically disqualifies the student
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Student is ineligible for a PGWP
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Proceed to assess other eligibility criteria

diagnostic_questions.question: For degree, college diploma, or graduate certificate programs: Does the student have CLB/NCLC 7 in all four language skills, and is the field of study IRCC-eligible?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the student meets the program-type-specific language and field of study requirements
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Student meets these additional eligibility criteria
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Student is ineligible for a PGWP if either the language threshold or field of study requirement is not met

diagnostic_questions.question: If the student transferred between DLIs, does the total time at DLIs amount to at least 8 months?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether combined DLI study time meets the minimum program length threshold
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Student meets the duration requirement for the transfer scenario
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Student is ineligible if total DLI time is under 8 months

industry_realities.common_belief: Any program at a Canadian school qualifies for a PGWP
industry_realities.actual_reality: Only programs at PGWP-eligible designated learning institutions (DLIs) qualify; programs at non-PGWP-eligible DLIs, non-Canadian institutions located in Canada, and private colleges under curriculum licensing agreements (after applicable cutoff dates) do not qualify
industry_realities.implication: Students must verify their specific institution AND program are PGWP-eligible before enrolling, not after completing the program

industry_realities.common_belief: Studying online from outside Canada counts the same as studying in Canada for PGWP purposes
industry_realities.actual_reality: For lock-in dates on or after September 1, 2024, only in-class study within Canada counts; time studied outside Canada is deducted from PGWP length. For earlier lock-in dates, transitional rules apply with different treatment for online-in-Canada vs. online-outside-Canada
industry_realities.implication: Students must track where they were physically located during all online coursework, as location — not just modality — determines PGWP impact

industry_realities.common_belief: A second Canadian degree entitles a graduate to a second PGWP
industry_realities.actual_reality: A PGWP can only be issued once per person; having already received a PGWP is an explicit disqualifier regardless of additional Canadian credentials earned
industry_realities.implication: Students who already used a PGWP must pursue alternative immigration pathways after completing a second Canadian program

industry_realities.common_belief: The 180-day application window begins after the student feels done with their program
industry_realities.actual_reality: The 180-day window begins from the date of official confirmation of program completion (e.g., official letter, transcript notation), not from the student's subjective sense of completion or from when final grades are received informally
industry_realities.implication: Students must track the official confirmation date precisely and apply promptly to avoid missing the deadline

industry_realities.common_belief: Taking a lighter course load in one semester to manage work or stress does not affect PGWP eligibility
industry_realities.actual_reality: Full-time enrollment is required in every semester; part-time is only permitted in the final semester. A single part-time non-final semester can disqualify the student
industry_realities.implication: Students considering a reduced load must exhaust all alternatives (medical deferrals, leaves of absence) rather than simply enrolling part-time mid-program

industry_realities.common_belief: Completing a program faster than its scheduled length means a shorter PGWP
industry_realities.actual_reality: If a student completes a program in less time than the normal length, they may be eligible for a PGWP valid for the full normal length of the program
industry_realities.implication: Students in accelerated programs should apply for the PGWP duration corresponding to the normal program length, not their actual completion time

industry_realities.common_belief: A program labeled under a public university's name is automatically PGWP-eligible
industry_realities.actual_reality: Programs delivered by a private career college under a curriculum licensing agreement with a public institution are generally NOT PGWP-eligible, with only narrow time-limited exceptions for programs started before specified cutoff dates
industry_realities.implication: Students must verify the delivery entity of their program, not just the branding, to confirm PGWP eligibility before enrolling

industry_realities.common_belief: Master's degree PGWP duration depends on the length of the master's program
industry_realities.actual_reality: Since February 2024, master's and doctoral degrees of any length receive a 3-year PGWP, regardless of whether the program was shorter than 2 years
industry_realities.implication: Students in accelerated or 1-year master's programs now receive the same 3-year PGWP as those in 2-year programs, changing the cost-benefit calculation of program length selection

junior_vs_senior_signals.naive_pattern: Checks only whether the institution is a 'Canadian university or college' and assumes any degree program qualifies
junior_vs_senior_signals.informed_pattern: Verifies the specific DLI is on the PGWP-eligible list, confirms the program is not delivered under a curriculum licensing agreement with a private college, and checks the field of study against IRCC's eligible fields list
junior_vs_senior_signals.why_it_matters: Enrollment at an ineligible institution or in an ineligible program type forfeits PGWP access entirely with no recourse after graduation

junior_vs_senior_signals.dimension: Understanding PGWP duration for master's programs
junior_vs_senior_signals.naive_pattern: Assumes a 1-year master's program yields only a 1-year PGWP and may choose a longer program solely to get a 3-year PGWP
junior_vs_senior_signals.informed_pattern: Knows that since February 2024, all master's and doctoral degrees receive a 3-year PGWP regardless of program length, making program length selection independent of PGWP duration for graduate students
junior_vs_senior_signals.why_it_matters: Students who are unaware of the February 2024 rule change may unnecessarily enroll in longer programs or incorrectly advise peers

junior_vs_senior_signals.naive_pattern: Starts the 180-day countdown from when they receive their degree parchment or feel finished with exams
junior_vs_senior_signals.informed_pattern: Identifies the exact date of official program completion confirmation from the institution and schedules PGWP application submission well before the 180-day deadline
junior_vs_senior_signals.why_it_matters: Missing the 180-day window results in permanent loss of PGWP eligibility for that program; there is no extension or appeal

junior_vs_senior_signals.dimension: Assessing distance learning impact on PGWP
junior_vs_senior_signals.naive_pattern: Treats all online courses the same regardless of where the student was physically located when taking them
junior_vs_senior_signals.informed_pattern: Tracks physical location during all online coursework; understands that post-September 1, 2024 lock-in date rules require in-class in-Canada study for at least 50% of the program and deduct outside-Canada time from PGWP duration
junior_vs_senior_signals.why_it_matters: Students who fail to track their physical location during online study may find their PGWP significantly shortened or be rendered ineligible

junior_vs_senior_signals.dimension: Advising students on second Canadian programs after PGWP use
junior_vs_senior_signals.naive_pattern: Tells a friend completing a second Canadian degree that they can get another PGWP after graduation
junior_vs_senior_signals.informed_pattern: Recognizes that the PGWP is a one-time benefit; advises the student to explore Express Entry, Provincial Nominee Programs, or spousal work permits instead
junior_vs_senior_signals.why_it_matters: Students who plan their immigration strategy around a second PGWP will find themselves without a work authorization pathway after completing their second program

junior_vs_senior_signals.naive_pattern: Advises a struggling student to simply take fewer courses for one semester to manage workload, unaware of PGWP implications
junior_vs_senior_signals.informed_pattern: Warns that part-time enrollment in any non-final semester violates PGWP full-time status requirements; recommends exploring medical deferrals, authorized leaves, or other IRCC-recognized exceptions instead
junior_vs_senior_signals.why_it_matters: A single non-final semester of part-time study can permanently disqualify an otherwise eligible student from the PGWP
